tests.exercises: In-crate cluster-operator tests cover reference-amplitude mapping, ranked exponential expansion, compact symmetry sectors, and fermionic spin-partition phases.
tests.why: The tests exercise deterministic amplitude and excitation algebra directly; pointwise comparison is appropriate because the compact finite vectors are deterministic and the expected coefficients are explicit.

tests.exercises: In-crate DIIS extrapolation and residual-cancellation test.
tests.why: The linear residual-cancellation invariant is deterministic and small; pointwise numerical comparison can detect an incorrect extrapolation without relying on a stochastic oracle.

tests.exercises: The CLI rank-series contract, committed primary CC(1)-CC(8) evidence, and stable JSON output for correlation-method calculations.
tests.why: The integration target drives the public cc-series entrypoint and compares energies, convergence metadata, and serialized fields; the calculations are deterministic for the fixed fixtures, so pointwise policy is the natural proposal.

tests.exercises: CC2, full-rank CC, warm-started CC series, invalid-rank/configuration rejection, and explicit termination across H2, H4, and H2O STO-3G fixtures.
tests.why: These official tests compare correlation energies and convergence behavior to FCI/PySCF or explicit failure contracts. The fixed small systems are deterministic; pointwise tolerances can be calibrated from nominal-versus-variant runs.

tests.exercises: CI variationality, MBPT(2) agreement with PySCF, UCC variational convergence, and warm-started CI-series behavior.
tests.why: The tests expose deterministic energies, variational inequalities, and convergence outcomes on finite H2/H4 systems. Pointwise policy is appropriate for the numerical observables; no random stream is involved.

tests.exercises: Published-reference CI/MBPT series and CLI reporting for the primary H2O/6-31G correlation benchmark.
tests.why: The official test compares order-by-order energies and residuals to committed literature/PySCF anchors. The fixture is deterministic; the initial check should use a shortened or lower-rank window if the full live series exceeds the three-minute investigation limit.
